threatFindings.threat: FF 1F CC CC INT87 searchers (OpcodeHunter1, 2B2Team1/2, ADDvanced1/2) hit our dwell anchors; low/spread decoys absorb their single-charge searches
threatFindings.evidence: Identical threat cohorts (base 0.5788 in all three jobs): dec0A (1 decoy at 0000h, B066 83rh4) +0.057; C1 (+ A natural tail decoy, wv8ov) +0.070; C2 (+3 more decoys at si+4000h/8000h/C000h, c1v5o) +0.085 [0.038,0.132]. Screens: s2025-15 (2B2Team) +0.233 / +0.367 / +0.467.
threatFindings.impact: About +0.05 to +0.16 per searcher cohort; about +0.01 on field S ALL (5/50 cohorts contain a searcher). The ordering dec0A < C1 < C2 is monotone but the step differences are within the CIs (no per-cohort pairing in the threat output), so 'more spread decoys are better' is supported but not proven.

threatFindings.threat: 2B2Team1 does not search from DI=0: it does INT86 at ES:DI=A500h first, so its INT87 starts at about A600h and wraps (the engine's int87 loops i=0..FFFF from DI with 16-bit wrap). A decoy only at 0000h is often not the first match
threatFindings.evidence: Static: dis86 of official-2025/survivors-online/TOM_2B2Team1 (mov di,A500h; int 86h; mov ax,1FFFh; mov dx,CCCCh; int 87h) plus Cpu.java int87/int86 (stosdw advances DI). Behavioural support: the largest gain from the spread decoys is on 2B2Team (+0.106 -> +0.163 threat, +0.233 -> +0.467 screen). This corrects B066's 'forward from DI=0' for 2B2Team.
threatFindings.impact: Explains why spread decoys help more than the single 0000h decoy

recommendation: promote-candidate: send A024-C2 (A only, agent2/night/scratch/A024/C2_A.asm, 143 B, sha 36bf5eee...) to confirmation as a defense add-on. Screen ALL +0.0169 [-0.0036,+0.0374] with no negative group; threat +0.085 vs the three FF1FCCCC searcher teams. Phoenix and INT87 timing equal rev0, and it only touches A, so it combines cleanly with B-side add-ons (B059 zph, B054 fix2steal); it replaces dec0A and stripA. Expect a pooled confirmation gain of only about +0.004 to +0.008 because searchers are rare (3/75 teams in 2025, 4/42 in 2024 live). It may not pass z=2.5 on its own, so it is a good part of a combination. Do not promote C1 separately (C2 contains it).
notes: Band-math equivalence: floor(si/3C00h)*3C00h + 2CA2h gives AH = floor(hi(si)/3Ch)*3Ch + 2Ch and AL = A2h, the same as rev0 for every si. Registers left differently at phoenix_init (CX, DX, flags) are all overwritten there. Template byte 17 becomes CCh (from 8Bh) as in stripA; the worker copy's tail is never a match because the trail byte A4 follows it. Decoy addresses relative to si never hit A itself.
